name: George Homer Allen
notable_stories: A brilliant lawyer who graduated Yale with Phi Beta Kappa honors
He traveled 17,000 miles across the U.S. and Canada by car in the 1980s
Led a long and successful effort to defeat the proposed LNG facility at Point Conception.
He led Montecito's first attempt at incorporation in the 1960s. He received the most votes in the election and would have been the city's first mayor had incorporation passed.
His interests were reading, gardening and travel. In the 1980s he and his wife spent a year travelling 17,000 miles through the U.S. and Canada in their motor home.
milestones: Married Dorothy Ann Wheeler (m. 8 May 1944, Sioux Falls, SD)
Married Suzzanne Modine (m. 22 Nov 1972, Las Vegas, NV)
Served as a Lieutenant in the Third Air Force during WWII
Father of five children from his first marriage
Lieutenant in Third Air Force during WWII
Military: Was overseas just after WWII and returned from Japan
Divorced from the preparer's mother (Dorothy Ann Wheeler)
Died 18 Sep 2010, Sarah House Hospice Center, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara County, CA

Military: After graduating enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Force; attended Air Force OCS in Florida; served in the 3rd Fighter Command; attended the School for Military Government (University of Virginia) and the Civil Affairs Training School (University of Michigan)
Military: After the Japanese surrender in 1945 he spent a year in Akita, Japan as a military government officer helping establish postwar democratization
Military: Lieutenant in the administration division of the Third Air Force, stationed at Sarasota, Florida (1944)
education: Bachelor of Arts in Government and Political Science from Yale University, 1943 (the obituary below gives 1942)
Juris Doctor from Harvard Law School, 1949
Attended Yale on a four-year regional scholarship, majored in Government, graduated with Exceptional Distinction in 1942
Graduated cum laude from Harvard Law School in 1949
Graduated from Yale University in 1942 with Phi Beta Kappa honors; majored in political science and was a member of the University Debate Association
career: Lawyer, described by his son as brilliant
Moved to California and started his law practice in Los Angeles
Moved to Santa Barbara in 1952 and practiced law, opening his own office in 1962
A general practitioner who became heavily involved in the planned development of The Hollister Ranch
Founded the law firm of Allen and Kimbell in 1980
locations: Sarah House Hospice Center, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara County, CA
